card.name: Punctuation ending quoted rhetorical questions
card.fires_on: Punctuation (mostly a question mark) that closes a rhetorical or challenging question in a quoted or religious passage. It also fires, more weakly, on digits in regulation numbers and on colons in Bible verse references.

modes.label: Rhetorical question mark
modes.description: A question mark ending a pointed question in a quotation, often biblical or philosophical.
modes.example: “How long are you going to be paralyzed by indecision<<?>> If the LORD is the true God,

modes.label: Citation numbers
modes.description: A digit or colon inside a regulation or scripture reference.

card.writes: The promoted tokens are mostly Chinese words for rhetorical questions such as 难道 and 是不是, so the pole adds a questioning, rhetorical tone.
card.plain: It marks the end of a pointed, rhetorical question, mostly in quoted or scriptural text.
